parts:
Hello!
Occasionally when analysing an Axivity AX6 accelerometry file, GGIR reports an error (fortunately it only happens occasionally).
 Here is the code I use (very similar to the code that is proposed by default when using this package)

setwd("/Users/marcosechevarriapolo/Desktop")
library(GGIR)
GGIR(mode=c(1,2,3,4,5),
     datadir="entrada",
     outputdir="salida",
     do.report=c(2,4,5),
     #=====================
     # Part 2
     #=====================
     data_masking_strategy = 1,
     hrs.del.start = 0,          hrs.del.end = 0,
     #maxdur = máximo de días a analizar, si es 1sem, poner 8
     maxdur = 16,                 includedaycrit = 16,
     qwindow=c(0,24),
     mvpathreshold =c(100),
     excludefirstlast = FALSE,
     includenightcrit = 16,
     #La siguiente línea es para las métricas MX, minutos más activos del día
     qlevels = c(c(960/1440),c(1320/1440),c(1380/1440),c(1410/1440),c(1425/1440),c(1430/1440),c(1435/1440),c(1438/1440)),
     #Con esta línea se reporta el gradiente de intensidad
     iglevels = TRUE,
     #=====================
     # Part 3 + 4
     #=====================
     def.noc.sleep = 1,
     outliers.only = TRUE,
     criterror = 4,
     do.visual = TRUE,
     #=====================
     # Part 5
     #=====================
     #La siguiente línea son los puntos de corte, cambiar según corresponda
     threshold.lig = c(40), threshold.mod = c(100),  threshold.vig = c(400),
     boutcriter = 0.8,      boutcriter.in = 0.9,     boutcriter.lig = 0.8,
     boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8, boutdur.in = c(1,10,30), boutdur.lig = c(1,10),
     boutdur.mvpa = c(1),
     includedaycrit.part5 = 2/3,
     do.sibreport = TRUE, #Analisis de la siesta
     #=====================
     # Visual report
     #=====================
     timewindow = c("WW"),
     visualreport=TRUE)

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] P3 file NAFilename not recognized
parts:
Hello Marcos,

As the error indicates: The file is empty or corrupt, which can happen.

To investigate:
  1. Identify a specific file that triggers the error.
  2. Read the file with GGIRread::readAxivity() function and check whether you can read at least some data from it.
  3. If 2 is not successful, read the file with other tools such as OMGUI or https://github.com/OxWearables/actipy to read cwa data and check whether that allows for reading the file.
  4. If 3 is successful and 2 is not then report this as an reproducible issue in https://github.com/wadpac/GGIRread. Otherwise it sounds like the file is truly corrupt or empty. Maybe the manufacturer can help you investigate further.

Thanks,

Vincent
